comments.body:
*[EIP-7979: Call and Return Opcodes for the EVM](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7979) Should be considered for inclusion in Hegotá.*

In the end the decision may be to not include this proposal in this fork.  We declined to consider this proposal for inclusion in the last fork, and I have made every effort since to engage with the reasons it was declined.  To not even consider this proposal for inclusion is not the best way to decide not to include it.

[EIP-7979](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7979) itself makes a strong argument for these industry-standard opcodes.  Two companion proposals strengthen the argument, and the prototypes and testing reported below answer questions about the difficulty of implementation and amount of technical debt.

* [EIP-7979: Call and Return Opcodes for the EVM](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7979)
Three instructions for building subroutines, an essential facility provided by almost all other blockchain VMs.
* [EIP-8173: Foundations of EVM Control Flow](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8173)
A brief tutorial on the VM and ZK fundamentals underlying these proposals, including why static control is essential.  Recommended reading.
* [EIP-8337: Validated EVM Code](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8337)
Subroutines are essential for meeting the static control flow requirements laid out in EIP-8173.  This proposal efficiently validates EIP-7979 code at CREATE time.  The reference validation takes less than five hundred lines of Python.

We now have EIP-7979 prototypes for [Solidity](https://github.com/argotorg/solidity/pull/17005), [Vyper](https://github.com/vyperlang/vyper/pull/5266), [geth](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/compare/master...gcolvin:go-ethereum:eip-7979), and [evmone](https://github.com/ipsilon/evmone/pull/1706) . (Thank you Claude.)  As detailed on the [Magicians' thread](
https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7979-call-and-return-opcodes-for-the-evm/24615/17?u=gcolvin) they don't take much space:  a _total_ of 466 lines of code, 130 lines of comments, and 679 lines of tests for _all four_.  

We also have reference specifications for implementation [EELS, EIP-7979](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3575) at 245 lines of code, docstrings, and comments, and 1,025 lines of tests, and also for validation [EELS, EIP-8337](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3576) at 445 lines of code, docstrings, and comments, and 606 lines of tests.

Neither is it a complex change, scoring at most 13 ([Preliminary Complexity Assessments for EIP-7979](https://github.com/ethspecs/pm/issues/72)) versus FOCIL at 15 and Frame Transactions at 38 ). Among execution-layer feature EIPs proposed for Hegotá, this is the smallest surface.

Only clients need to make any immediate changes.  Compilers and other tools can adopt this EIP on their own schedule.

EIP-8337 could have been included in this fork, but discussions on previous calls and the breakout indicate to me that it belongs in a later fork, after we have gained more experience with EIP-7979.  The prototype implementations of EIP-7979 generate 8337-compliant code.

Re: [EIP-8163](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8163) "Reserve `EXTENSION (0xae)` opcode"

ACD asked for feedback from L2s and Alt-L1s to voice support for this it before considering it. Offchain definitely supports including this EIP. One reason we don't currently consider adding opcodes to Arbitrum Nitro is that such a reserved opcode doesn't exist.

Staying on the subject of [EIP-8163](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8163), I would like to add advancing it to CFI to the agenda.

As requested, I posted demand examples in: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8163-reserve-extension-0xae-opcode/27756/8. tl;dr: EIP-8163 exists to unblock R&D on EVM extensions in the first place, and there are already examples to name: Monad's MIP-4, MIP-8, execution designs on top of Cadence, and flexible account authentication. All of these consider or have considered adding custom opcodes. [MIP-7](https://mips.monad.xyz/MIPs/MIP-7) is Monad's framework spec for deploying opcodes on top of EIP-8163.

Outside Monad, Rootstock and Tron have or had custom opcodes, and per [comment above](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2223#issuecomment-5719895334), Arbitrum Nitro would also like to see the reservation.
